subject: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@stardata.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Stardata Finance <finance@stardata.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos@stardata.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re well — we rolled through a surprise spike over the long weekend and exceeded our provisioned quota by roughly 2.3x for ~6 hours. That triggered the standard overrun pricing and the bill is going to be painful for the month.

Before we proceed with the invoice, we wanted to ask whether Redwood has a short-term contingency mechanism we can lean on for situations like this — ideally something that: (a) caps our exposure for a defined window, (b) doesn’t force us to take a long-term commit immediately, and (c) gives us a path to a discount if we convert to a higher committed tier later this quarter.

Attached is an anonymized usage dump for the spike window (usage_report_July13.csv). For context: the spike is product-driven, not an attack — we expect it could repeat for short bursts over next 90 days as we ramp a new feature.

Can you outline options (cap, fixed contingency fee, prepaid buffer, short-term blended surcharge) and any impacts to invoicing / credits? We’re open to a limited-duration fee if that’s necessary to avoid full overrun rates.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it’s easier.

— Elena
Head of Platform, Stardata
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@stardata.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal

Hi Elena — thanks for the data and the note. Sorry you hit that unexpected spike. We have a few pragmatic options we typically offer for short windows like this:

1) 72-hour contingency credit: customer prepays a capped buffer (refundable for unused portion) that covers up to X tokens/day at a blended surcharge. This avoids triggering overrun tiers on the invoice.
2) Temporary blended surcharge: apply a capped surcharge multiplier to spike tokens (for example 1.35x base rate) up to an agreed ceiling, then revert to normal billing.
3) Prepaid minute-scale buffer: a small, non-refundable buffer purchased by the minute/hour for very short spikes — useful for predictable, short-lived pulses.
4) Commit conversion discount path: if you convert to a 3-month committed plan within 30 days, we can offer a staged discount (10–20% depending on size) applied retroactively to contested spike charges up to the contingency cap.

To give you a concrete starter: if you’re looking to limit exposure for the 6-hour event, we can offer a 3-day contingency credit sized at your estimated peak token rate, billed upfront as a single line item (we’ll credit unused amounts). If Stardata is willing to move to a monthly committed slab above your current baseline, we can attach a 15% committed discount on the next quarter and apply a partial rebate to the contingency buffer.

I’m looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (billing) to make sure the structure is workable from both commercial and accounting sides. Ben/Laura — can you weigh in on the preferred phrasing and whether we should push for prepaid vs. simple surcharge?

If you want, we can also draft a short DocuSign that sets the cap, window, and refund rules so you have clear visibility into invoicing.

Best,
Irene
Director, Enterprise Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal

Quick internal notes — I like keeping the option set small and explicit to avoid scope creep. My recommended commercial structure:

- Name: Stability Surcharge + Contingency Credit
- Window: up to 72 contiguous hours (customer chooses start time)
- Billing: prepaid contingency credit equal to forecasted peak tokens * blended rate; unused credit refundable within 30 days as a single-line credit (helps with customer trust)
- Surcharge cap: surcharge multiplier of 1.5x on tokens consumed beyond baseline but within the buffer window; beyond buffer, standard overrun pricing applies
- Discount kicker: convert to a 3-month commit >= X tokens/month within 30 days and receive 12–18% discount (tiered) on the next quarter; retroactive application up to the contingency buffer amount

Operational notes: we should avoid a permanently discounted overrun rate — structure needs an expiration clause and explicit non-precedence language. Also propose a short escalation clause: if spikes become recurring (3 events in a 60-day window), we open a renewal conversation instead of automatic renewals.

Irene — if you want, I can draft the wording for the DocuSign and a short line-item for the invoice.

— Ben
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:20:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal

Finance perspective: prepaid credit with a clear refund policy is the cleanest from an invoicing and revenue recognition standpoint. A few specifics to include in the DocuSign/quote so accounting can process cleanly: 

- Label the line: "Contingency Credit (72-hr window) — refundable unused balance within 30 days"
- Show the base price, surcharge multiplier used for blended rate, and separate the potential retroactive discount line so it’s contingent on commit conversion (do not book the discount until conversion occurs)
- Limit the refundable window to 30 days after the buffer window closes to simplify reconciliations
- Cap the maximum refundable amount to the prepaid buffer (no add-ons)

I also want to see a conservative token estimate for the proposed 72-hour buffer (please include expected max QPS and avg tokens per request). If the customer expects sustained multi-hour spikes more than twice in a 60-day window, prefer converting them to a short-term committed slab instead of repeated buffers — easier to forecast revenue.

Happy to approve the prepaid-credit path once we have the numbers.

— Laura
Director, Finance — Commercial Billing
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@stardata.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 15:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity stabilization fee and staggered discount proposal

Thanks everyone — Elena, based on your spike and our internal take, here’s a concise proposal for Stardata: 

1) 72-hour Contingency Credit (prepaid): we’ll size the buffer to 3x your baseline daily tokens (you provided numbers in the CSV). Preliminary quote: $12,500 for the 72-hour buffer. Unused balance refundable within 30 days of buffer end.

2) Stability surcharge: during the buffer window, spike tokens are billed at a blended surcharge of 1.35x the base rate up to the prepaid cap. Beyond the cap, standard overrun tiers apply.

3) Commit conversion discount: if Stardata upgrades to a 3-month commit at or above the new baseline within 30 days, Redwood will apply a 15% discount to the next quarter and will retroactively credit up to $6,250 against the contingency buffer (i.e., up to 50% of the buffer amount).

4) Governance: clause that if spikes occur 3+ times in a 60-day rolling window we’ll trigger a renewal/commit conversation (no automatic renewal of contingency credits).

Attached is a short contingency quote (contingency_quote_Stardata.pdf) and a DocuSign template link for the prepaid credit. If that looks acceptable, Elena, please reply with approval or a suggested alternate cap and we’ll get DocuSign over. If you prefer a surcharge-only approach (no prepay), we can provide that as an alternate but it requires a slightly higher multiplier.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Irene
Director, Enterprise Partnerships
Redwood Inference
